items.title: 14.5.2 Impact of deforestation on the atmosphere

source_refs.note: Topic 14.5.2 as printed, with Quick Check 14.2 printed at its end, printed page 311.

blocks.text: Deforestation is purposeful cleaning or thinning of forests by humans. Deforestation represents one of the largest issues in global climate. Forests absorb GHGs like CO₂ and clean air for us. In short, deforestation has a wide range of negative impact on the environment, including loss of biodiversity climate change, soil degradation, and water cycle disruption.

blocks.prompt: a) Mention man-made sources of air pollution.
blocks.explanation: Mobile sources: cars, trucks, aircraft and ship engines. Point sources: factories and power stations. All of these burn fossil fuels and release CO₂, CO and hydrocarbons. Burning wood in homes and coal in brick kilns are also man-made sources.

blocks.prompt: b) How do polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) primarily enter the atmosphere?
blocks.explanation: Through the incomplete combustion of fossil fuels (coal, oil, petrol) and wood: vehicle exhaust, industrial processes, open fires and grilling food. Some also come from the natural seepage of petroleum and coal.

blocks.prompt: c) How do volatile organic compounds (VOCs) affect air quality?
blocks.explanation: VOCs enter the air as gases from liquid fuels, exhaust, and burning wood and waste, and they pollute both indoor and outdoor air. In the short term they cause irritation of the eyes, nose and throat, headache and nausea; in the long term they damage the liver, kidneys and nervous system. In sunlight they also react with NOₓ to form smog.

blocks.prompt: d) What are major sources of heavy metals in the atmosphere?
blocks.explanation: Metallurgy, battery waste and incineration (burning of waste), as well as industrial processes and transport.
